regimens.indication: Acute Ischemic Stroke (NIHSS <= 5) or High-Risk TIA (Loading Dose)

refs.locator: Section 1.3 Acute Ischemic Stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA)
refs.quote: BRILINTA is indicated to reduce the risk of stroke in patients with acute ischemic stroke (NIH Stroke Scale score ≤5) or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA) [see Clinical Studies (14.3) ] .

refs.locator: Section 2.4 Acute Ischemic Stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA)
refs.quote: Initiate treatment with a 180 mg loading dose of BRILINTA and then continue with 90 mg twice daily for up to 30 days. Administer the first maintenance dose 6 to 12 hours after the loading dose. Use BRILINTA with a loading dose of aspirin (300 mg to 325 mg) and a daily maintenance dose of aspirin of 75 mg to 100 mg [see Clinical Studies (14) ].

regimens.dose_text: Initiate treatment with a single 180 mg oral loading dose of BRILINTA, administered with a loading dose of aspirin (300 mg to 325 mg).

refs.locator: Section Use in Specific Populations / Clinical Pharmacology
refs.quote: Renal Impairment No dosage adjustment is needed in patients with renal impairment [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ] . Patients with End-Stage Renal Disease on dialysis Clinical efficacy and safety studies with BRILINTA did not enroll patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on dialysis.

hepatic.value: Ticagrelor is metabolized by the liver and impaired hepatic function can increase risks for bleeding and other adverse events. Avoid use of BRILINTA in patients with severe hepatic impairment. There is limited experience with BRILINTA in patients with moderate hepatic impairment; consider the risks and benefits of treatment, noting the probable increase in exposure to ticagrelor. No dosage adjustment is needed in patients with mild hepatic impairment.

value: WARNING: BLEEDING RISK: BRILINTA, like other antiplatelet agents, can cause significant, sometimes fatal bleeding. Do not use BRILINTA in patients with active pathological bleeding or a history of intracranial hemorrhage. Do not start BRILINTA in patients undergoing urgent coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG). If possible, manage bleeding without discontinuing BRILINTA. Stopping BRILINTA increases the risk of subsequent cardiovascular events.

refs.quote: BRILINTA, like other antiplatelet agents, can cause significant, sometimes fatal bleeding ( 5.1 , 6.1 ). Do not use BRILINTA in patients with active pathological bleeding or a history of intracranial hemorrhage ( 4.1 , 4.2 ). Do not start BRILINTA in patients undergoing urgent coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) ( 5.1 , 6.1 ).
Ticagrelor and its major metabolite reversibly interact with the platelet P2Y 12 ADP-receptor to prevent signal transduction and platelet activation.

mg_safety.note: Antiplatelet agents do not impair neuromuscular junction transmission; safe in myasthenia gravis

value.instructions: For patients who are unable to swallow tablets whole, BRILINTA tablets can be crushed, mixed with water, and drunk. The mixture can also be administered via a nasogastric tube (CH8 or greater).

missed_dose.value: Advise patients who miss a dose of BRILINTA to take their next dose at its scheduled time.

refs.quote: Advise patients who miss a dose of BRILINTA to take their next dose at its scheduled time.

reversal.dose: Supportive care; ticagrelor is not dialyzable
reversal.notes: There is currently no known treatment to reverse the effects of BRILINTA, and ticagrelor is not dialyzable. Platelet transfusion did not reverse the antiplatelet effect of BRILINTA in healthy volunteers and is unlikely to be of clinical benefit in patients with bleeding.

refs.quote: There is currently no known treatment to reverse the effects of BRILINTA, and ticagrelor is not dialyzable. Treatment of overdose should follow local standard medical practice. Bleeding is the expected pharmacologic effect of overdosing. If bleeding occurs, appropriate supportive measures should be taken. Platelet transfusion did not reverse the antiplatelet effect of BRILINTA in healthy volunteers and is unlikely to be of clinical benefit in patients with bleeding.

lactation_summary.value: Breastfeeding is not recommended during ticagrelor treatment.

refs.quote: There are no data on the presence of ticagrelor or its metabolites in human milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production.

value.drug_or_class: Strong CYP3A Inhibitors & Inducers (Ketoconazole, Rifampin, Carbamazepine)
value.effect: Strong CYP3A inhibitors markedly elevate ticagrelor exposure and bleeding risk; strong CYP3A inducers markedly decrease ticagrelor exposure and antiplatelet efficacy.
value.management: Avoid concomitant use of ticagrelor with strong CYP3A inhibitors or strong CYP3A inducers.

refs.quote: Avoid use with strong CYP3A inhibitors or CYP3A inducers.

value.effect: Co-administration of opioids delays and reduces the absorption and systemic exposure of ticagrelor, blunting early platelet inhibition.
value.management: In acute coronary syndromes requiring opioid analgesia, consider use of a parenteral antiplatelet agent.

refs.quote: Opioids: Decreased exposure to ticagrelor. Consider use of parenteral anti-platelet agent.

value.effect: Ticagrelor increases exposure to simvastatin and lovastatin, elevating the risk of statin-induced myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
value.management: Limit doses of simvastatin and lovastatin to no more than 40 mg daily when coadministered with ticagrelor.

refs.quote: Patients receiving more than 40 mg per day of simvastatin or lovastatin may be at increased risk of statin-related adverse effects.
Avoid use with strong CYP3A inhibitors or CYP3A inducers.
